name: Jeremy D. Brown
title: John C. Malone Associate Professor
fitReason: A medical-HRI and haptic interaction match with an attributable collaborative experiment connecting a pretrained visual model to real robot control. The current lab emphasis is broader haptics and human perception, so a CS-heavy short project needs explicit alignment.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full August 2025 TMRB paper uses CoTracker visual tracking with an RGB-D camera to update a fuzzy controller on an actual KUKA LBR Med during ex vivo porcine-tissue cutting. Initial landmarks are manually selected, and path planning is geometric. Six closed-loop cuts were compared with three open-loop cuts. The learned tracker operates online, but its 2.9-fps rate and reliance on calibration limit translation; this is not validated clinical autonomy. Brown is a coauthor. The inspected current HAMR member list does not establish this experiment as a current independently led Brown-group platform, so it is scored as collaborative hardware.

shortVisit.summary: The live HAMR Join Us page welcomes undergraduate and master’s participation, but its linked detailed guidance is explicitly dated September 15, 2016 and focuses on JHU research courses with a two-semester fall/spring commitment. It encourages full-time summer research without establishing current external-master’s eligibility. Listed summer REU/PURA pathways are undergraduate-specific. No current external eight-week or summer 2027 invitation was verified.
